games\UFC5\bin\UFC 5.exe and UFC 5 AMD.exe - licence, credits and source
=========================================================================

games\UFC5\bin\UFC 5.exe and games\UFC5\bin\UFC 5 AMD.exe are two Windows x64 builds of KytyPS5, a free
and open-source PlayStation 5 translation layer, from Cozma's fork made to run EA SPORTS UFC 5
(PPSA03541), with roshanarunk's UFC 5 work merged into it. No game files are included: you need your
own dump of the game. UFC5.exe starts UFC 5 AMD.exe on an AMD video card and UFC 5.exe on the others
(engine_amd=0 in UFC5.ini makes it use UFC 5.exe on AMD too).

UFC 5.exe is Cozma's own build of 2026-10-25 (ThinLTO and profile-guided optimization), unchanged except
for the renaming and the one-jump change described below. Its version line names commit 7a6db0ec with local changes; those
changes are the ones published as commit 84f029fe.

UFC 5 AMD.exe is PORTHEON's build (clang-cl, Release, ThinLTO, as the project's CI) of commit 84f029fe
with games\UFC5\src\ufc5-motor-amd321.patch (PORTHEON 4.0.3, completed in 4.0.4), which changes these
things:
  - a fault or a failure of the video driver while it compiles a pipeline no longer closes the game
    ("error 321" on AMD cards): the pipeline is built again without the driver's optimization, and
    if that fails too, its draws or dispatches are skipped;
  - the same for the engine's own helper pipelines (texture tiling, blits, clears, the video-out
    overlay...); on AMD cards those start without the driver's optimization, and the texture tiling
    shaders go to the driver in variants with their specialization constants fixed in the source
    (compiled by glslang with scripts/portheon_bake_tiler.py, included in the patch);
  - a player name longer than the game's buffer is shortened at a whole character instead of closing
    the game.

PORTHEON then renamed both files and changed how they present themselves: the UFC 5 icon and a version
block naming them "UFC 5", the window title (the format string of the title, padded with zero bytes:
"UFC 5" up to PORTHEON 4.3.0, "UFC 5 | frame: N, fps: F" from 4.3.1, which UFC5.exe reads to set the
game's speed from the real FPS) and the Windows GUI subsystem (no console window). The tool that does
this is games\UFC5\src\brand_engine.c (with ufc5-engine.rc); _build-tools retitle_engine.py made the
4.3.1 title change on the files of 4.3.0. The engine's code is not changed by any of this.

One change to the code itself, from PORTHEON 4.3.1 (2026-10-30), in both files: the video-out status the
engine gives the game (sceVideoOutGetOutputStatus) reports a 4K screen only when the engine's own screen
(--screen-width/--screen-height) is 4K, and a 1080p screen below that. The engine already decides it
this way for games whose param.json has bit 0x4 of ATTRIBUTE3; the change takes that branch for every
game. Before it, UFC 5 always believed it was on a 4K TV and rendered at 2136x1200 for a 3200x1800 FSR2
output; on a 1080p or 1440p screen it now renders its 1080p mode (1068x600 for a 1600x900 FSR2 output),
like a PS5 on a 1080p TV. It is one conditional jump of that function: at file offset 0x10c99a2 of UFC 5.exe
"jne" becomes "jmp" (75 6a -> eb 6a), and at 0xee4614 of UFC 5 AMD.exe "je" becomes two no-ops
(74 13 -> 90 90). The files keep their size and date.

Credits for this build, as the PORTHEON author gives them: Cozmaa and Brotski, whose UFC 5 build of
KytyPS5 PORTHEON improved (the AMD build above, the game's speed set from the real FPS, the crowd,
shadows and seats switches, the audio watchdog off).

Licence
-------
KytyPS5 is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 2 (licenses\LICENSE-GPL-2.0.txt).
Parts of the original Kyty code are under the MIT licence (Kyty-MIT.txt in this folder). The FFmpeg
and Opus libraries built into it are under their own licences (ffmpeg\ and opus\ in this folder).

Copyright: the KytyPS5 developers (https://github.com/KytyPS5/KytyPS5), InoriRus (Kyty), Cozma
(cozma-ufc5 fork), roshanarunk (UFC 5 work merged into it), Senaxx (Vulkan recording thread, draw
preparation scanner, shader disk cache, VRAM budget) and EmK530 (renderer optimizations, through
Senaxx's fork).

Source
------
Complete corresponding source code of both builds:
  https://github.com/Cozmaaa/KytyPS5/tree/cozma-ufc5
  commit 84f029fe52077feb7fc85e89ee273d57b2486a24
  ("ufc5: fewer GPU stalls, own CPU cores, PGO build, lighter GPU thread", 2026-10-25)
plus, for UFC 5 AMD.exe, games\UFC5\src\ufc5-motor-amd321.patch (applied on that commit), and for both,
brand_engine.c and ufc5-engine.rc for the changes described above and the video-out jump described there.

Written offer: for at least three years from the date of this release, PORTHEON also provides the
complete corresponding source code of these builds to anyone who received them, on request through
the PORTHEON project page (github.com/XAndromedaXR/PORTHEON).

Requirements: Windows 10/11 x64, a Vulkan 1.3 GPU with current drivers, a processor with AVX2 and the
Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022 Redistributable (x64), 2019 or newer.

This project is not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment or Electronic Arts.
